description: What a control-plane error carries when the API answers a request with an error status. The API answers every refusal with a Problem+JSON body, and many carry structured fields beside their sentence -- a platform_image_required 403 names refused_images, allowed_images and allowed_repositories; a plan_limit 403 names resource, limit and used. Every SDK's API error exposes: status, the HTTP status; problem, the whole body parsed, exactly when it is a JSON object (null for a body that is empty, not JSON, or JSON that is not an object), so any structured field is reachable without a new SDK release; code, the body's code when it is a string with a non-whitespace character, else the code inside a detail that is itself an object (FastAPI's own envelope, which the API's Problem+JSON handler normally lifts), else null; and detail, read the same way from the detail member -- the whole sentence exactly as sent, never trimmed, collapsed or shortened. A message built for display may be shortened, but it never carries a value the body echoed back from the request: every string in message_excludes must be absent from the error's message and its string form -- whatever key the echoed value sits under and whatever its shape, since a validation error's input is the request as sent, not a field a key-name filter can recognise (an SDK or tool that prints a validation error's entries prints each input as "[omitted]"). Each case's response is the status, the Content-Type and the body text the API sent; expect is what the SDK's error exposes, recorded as {status, code, detail, problem}.
